absent: Numeric values and bit positions for page-table descriptors, protection bits, masks, contiguity counts and tag-storage sizes are not shown in these fragments.
Implementation of the table allocator callback, its backing memory, concurrency control and failure modes beyond the invalid-address sentinel is not shown.
EFI descriptor layout, virtual mapping guarantees, misalignment predicate and page-range walker mechanics are not shown.
Floating-point, vector and matrix state structures, firmware address-space helpers and TTBR0 access primitives are not shown.
Coredump walker helpers for page lookup, emission, skipping and page-flag interpretation are not shown.
Interrupt-stack provisioning, per-CPU pointer layout, shadow-stack handling and syndrome decoding are not shown.
Scheduler, preemption, RCU, lock-dependency and tracing primitives referenced by entry and debug paths are not shown.
Multiprocessor ordering, barrier requirements beyond deferred walker visibility, and early-mapping lock discipline are not shown.

findings.text: Two public installers publish large-block entries at different table levels from a physical base plus caller-supplied protection adjusted to section form. Each first validates that the transition from the current slot content to the proposed entry only alters permission attributes, rejects unsafe changes with a failure indication, enforces required base alignment, and otherwise makes the new entry visible and reports success.

An early-boot helper revises permissions over an EFI runtime region already mapped at page granularity. It accepts a memory-management context, a firmware descriptor and a branch-target-identification flag, requires a runtime code or data region type, silently succeeds without action on misaligned regions, and otherwise walks the virtual span derived from the recorded page count applying a per-leaf updater with caller context.

Two small EFI utilities are exposed: one reports whether firmware runtime services remain available for power control, and another records a rate-limited firmware defect diagnostic when a reserved register is clobbered across a runtime call while forwarding the original firmware status unchanged to the caller.

A paired setup and teardown interface brackets every virtual firmware runtime invocation. Setup asserts the runtime lock, selects between a migratable-thread path and a direct map-load path, preserves floating-point state, and enables user-access mappings with an errata barrier. Teardown reverses those effects in a safe order that avoids premature activation of user tables.

A paired floating-point preservation interface guards firmware calls. The begin operation is inert without hardware support, otherwise uses a kernel-mode entry path when SIMD use is permitted and a diagnostic plus task-termination plus base-state save path when invoked from atomic context. The end operation restores state through the matching mechanism.

A fault-recovery hook decides whether an exception originated inside a firmware runtime service by combining a per-context firmware flag with a fault-address range check. On a match it logs a firmware defect, marks the kernel tainted for firmware workaround, disables further runtime services, redirects the saved return value and program counter toward a recovery stub, and preserves an extra register under shadow-stack builds.

A global pointer designates the top of a dedicated firmware-runtime stack and carries a post-initialization read-only protection attribute, so it is writable during early setup and immutable thereafter. Provisioning allocates a thread-sized virtual stack, disables runtime services with a warning on exhaustion, and otherwise publishes the top address.

Four coredump helpers extend standard notes with memory-tag data: a counter of tag-bearing mappings, a program-header writer that chains file offsets across those mappings, a size accumulator for the extra payload, and a payload writer that dumps each tagged range in order and aborts the dump on first failure.

A heap allocator provides a buffer sized for the tag set of one memory page, using blocking kernel allocation semantics. Callers use a single such buffer across an entire range dump and release it afterwards.

Early table construction descends strictly through levels without ever encountering a leaf where a table is expected. An empty upper slot demands a table allocator callback, fails cleanly when the allocator is missing or reports an invalid address, and otherwise installs a fresh cleared table with restrictive execute and accessed attributes before proceeding into it. A populated upper slot is validated for table form and reused through a temporary mapping.

Promotion to a contiguous hint requires joint alignment of virtual start, chunk end and physical base to the relevant contiguity granularity, plus absence of a caller-supplied contiguity veto and absence of any already-valid non-contiguous entry within the surrounding chunk. When all three hold, the leaf protection gains the contiguous attribute; otherwise the original protection is retained.

At the intermediate level a large-block entry is chosen only for a fully aligned chunk when block mappings are permitted and the existing slot is not already a table; all other cases descend to the next level. Once any leaf or block slot has been populated, later updates are confined to permission attributes, with violations treated as fatal programming errors and unexpected value changes flagged during development.

Temporary mappings mediate all table access during early construction and are released exactly once per range operation after the iteration completes or aborts. Leaf writes use a non-synchronizing store whose visibility to the hardware walker is deferred to the barrier effects that accompany release of the temporary mapping.

Per-leaf firmware permission revision honors firmware-supplied attributes: a read-only attribute forces the read-only bit, an execute-prohibit attribute forces the privileged-execute-never bit, and only when execution remains allowed may branch-target protection be applied subject to both hardware support and a per-region capability flag. Updates preserve all other leaf bits.

Memory-tag coredump support activates only on capable hardware and selects exactly those recorded mappings bearing the tag-enabled flag. Both header count and payload size derive from that filtered set, with each mapping contributing tag storage proportional to its dumpable page count.

Tag dumping proceeds page by page with graceful handling of absent or untagged pages by advancing the output offset without emitting data. Tagged pages share one lazily allocated staging buffer that is filled from hardware and emitted sequentially; allocation or emission failure terminates the range with an error indication while still releasing the staging buffer.

Kernel-mode and user-mode transitions pair generic context tracking with architecture-specific memory-tag and matrix-extension handling. Entry from kernel checks fault status and suppresses tag checking; exits to kernel mask asynchronous faults before checking status. User paths add resume-state notes on entry and order interrupt masking, preparation, extension exit and tag checks before final return.

Debug entry from the privileged level records the prior interrupt-enabled state, then unconditionally marks interrupts disabled for lock tracking and enters non-maskable context with tracing closure. Exit mirrors those effects conditionally on the recorded state, restoring tracing and lock state only when entry observed them enabled.

System-call boundaries manage vector state lazily. Entry leaves matrix payload untouched while exiting streaming mode where supported, discards live vector state for vector-enabled threads, and arms a per-CPU marker so later saves can skip extended state. Exit is inert without vector support and otherwise clears the marker to resume full preservation once state is bound again.

A per-CPU flag serializes a single-step erratum workaround around system calls. The active build engages only for threads flagged for single-step on affected CPUs, temporarily enabling single-step and kernel-debug controls with a debug unmask and barrier, then restores the original control value and clears the flag. The consume path handles only flagged CPUs by masking debug faults. Alternate builds replace both directions with inert stubs.

The permission-update carrier pairs an immutable reference to a firmware memory descriptor with a boolean indicating branch-target capability for the region. The descriptor supplies type, attributes, virtual base and page count used by the walker; the flag gates application of guarded-page protection.

Firmware invocation moves through locked setup, mapped execution and ordered teardown. Setup acquires the runtime context via one of two mutually exclusive branches, then preserves vector state and opens user-access mappings. Execution runs with migration pinned on the thread path. Teardown restores vector state, closes user access before releasing the mapping context, and unpins migration where applicable.

Range installation advances monotonically from start toward end in level-appropriate chunks, updating table position by index delta and physical base by consumed length. Each chunk either completes its leaf or table work and continues, or aborts the whole range on allocation or descent failure with cleanup of temporary mappings before reporting the error.

Synchronous dispatch preserves the previous interrupt register context, selects execution stack based on current stack identity, invokes the handler on the chosen stack, and finally restores the saved context. The stack-switching helper itself saves the asynchronous mask and shadow state, establishes a frame, calls through to the per-CPU stack top, then reconstitutes the original stack, frame and masks.

Extra-segment production follows count, header emission with running file-offset accumulation, size summation and payload emission phases over the same filtered mapping set. Header and size phases are pure computations; payload emission performs storage access and can fail, in which case the overall extra-data operation fails without attempting later mappings.

Assembly-visible control transfers include a user-return trampoline that funnels into the system-call exit path with interrupts managed internally, and a family of generated fault handlers that capture the syndrome register and delegate to a common unhandled-exception routine which never returns normally.

Two low-level routines are callable from assembly: a stack-switching dispatcher that executes a supplied handler on the dedicated interrupt stack and returns to the caller, and a tag harvesting routine that compacts architectural tag values from one page into a sequential destination buffer.

Firmware runtime entry requires the caller to already hold the runtime lock and pins the calling thread against migration while the firmware address space is borrowed, releasing the pin only after the borrowed context is relinquished. The non-thread path instead assumes exclusive use of a preloaded firmware mapping without migration control.

Debug exception handling runs with preemption disabled across the critical region and re-enabled without immediate rescheduling on exit, while asserting that read-copy-update observation remains active on entry.

Descending into a leaf entry, reusing a malformed table entry, or missing a required table allocator indicates a fatal construction bug. Attempting to alter more than permission bits in an already populated slot likewise aborts, and physical misalignment for large-block installation is flagged as a virtual-memory bug.

Invoking firmware runtime from hard-interrupt or non-maskable context triggers a rate-limited warning and forced termination of the current task, preserving only base floating-point state on the assumption normal execution cannot resume. Unhandled privileged exceptions escalate to a panic after register dump, while recoverable firmware faults taint the kernel and permanently disable runtime services.

Exhaustion during early table allocation or dedicated-stack provisioning fails gracefully: table growth reports a memory-exhaustion error to abort the range, and stack allocation warns, disables firmware runtime services and propagates the same exhaustion error while leaving the system operational without runtime calls.

Three caller-supplied vetoes govern early mapping construction. The executable veto is identified as NO_EXEC_MAPPINGS. The contiguity veto is identified as NO_CONT_MAPPINGS. The block veto is identified as NO_BLOCK_MAPPINGS. The invalid address sentinel is identified as INVALID_PHYS_ADDR. The exhaustion code is identified as ENOMEM.

Contiguity handling uses chunk counts and alignment masks plus a leaf attribute. The page-level count is identified as CONT_PTES. The intermediate-level count is identified as CONT_PMDS. One alignment mask is identified as CONT_PTE_MASK. Another is identified as CONT_PMD_MASK. Block alignment uses PMD_MASK at one level. Block alignment uses PUD_MASK at the higher level. The leaf hint bit is identified as PTE_CONT.

Firmware permission handling references descriptor types and attributes plus page-table bits. One runtime type is identified as EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES_CODE. Another is identified as EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES_DATA. The read-only attribute is identified as EFI_MEMORY_RO. The execute-prohibit attribute is identified as EFI_MEMORY_XP. One target bit is identified as PTE_RDONLY. Another is identified as PTE_PXN. An optional guarded bit is identified as PTE_GP.

Tag coredump and stack provisioning use fixed sizes and types. Per-page tag storage is identified as MTE_PAGE_TAG_STORAGE. The extra program-header type is identified as PT_AARCH64_MEMTAG_MTE. Tag-enabled mappings are selected by VM_MTE. Firmware stack allocation uses THREAD_SIZE. Interrupt displacement uses IRQ_STACK_SIZE.

Exception and workaround control uses processor-state and debug bits plus status codes. The debug-mask bit is identified as PSR_D_BIT. Single-step enable is identified as MDSCR_EL1_SS. Kernel-debug enable is identified as MDSCR_EL1_KDE. Forced termination uses SIGKILL. Firmware abort uses EFI_ABORTED.
